svg.text: AMAZON — THE CHECKOUT SAGA (ALL OR NOTHING)
THE HAPPY PATH — reserve BEFORE the order exists
① GUARD — empty cart is not an order
if (cartItems.isEmpty()) throw new EmptyCartException(customerId);
before the fix an empty cart produced a valid order with 0 items and a total of 0
② RESERVE EVERY LINE — and log what you took
List<CartItem> reserved = new ArrayList<>(); // the compensation log
for (CartItem item : cartItems) {
Product p = products.getProduct(item.getProductId());
if (p == null) throw new ProductNotFoundException(...);
if (!p.tryReserve(item.getQuantity()))
throw new InsufficientStockException(...);
reserved.add(item); items.add(new OrderItem(... price SNAPSHOT ...)); }
stock leaves the catalog HERE, atomically per product, before any order exists ✓
③ CREATE THE ORDER — only now
orderId = orders.createOrder(customerId, items, address); // status = PENDING
order-first would leave a phantom order to clean up when a reservation fails ✓
④ CLEAR THE CART, RETURN THE ORDER ID
cart.clearCart(customerId); return orderId;
WHERE PAYMENT GOES — and why the order matters
Charge first ⇒ you take money for an order you cannot fulfil.
Confirm first ⇒ you ship goods you were not paid for.
If the charge fails, release the reservation — same compensation.
honest: PaymentService here always approves; only the ORDERING is designed
THE FAILURE PATH — compensate, then rethrow
a 3-line cart where line 3 is short
line 1: tryReserve(2) → true → reserved = [1]
line 2: tryReserve(1) → true → reserved = [1, 2]
line 3: tryReserve(5) → FALSE → InsufficientStockException
catch (RuntimeException e) {
releaseAll(reserved); // undo lines 1 and 2
throw e; } // no order, no partial reservation
THIS IS THE SAGA PATTERN IN MINIATURE
No distributed transaction. Just: record what you did, so you can undo it.
The reserved list IS the compensation log. Same shape as the
ministore order saga elsewhere in this repo.
Distributed version: ReserveInventory → ChargePayment → ConfirmOrder,
one compensating action per step, plus an outbox for reliable events.
HONEST LIMIT: compensation is not atomic. A crash between the reserve and
the release leaks stock — that is what a reconciliation job is for.
all-or-nothing also means a 20-item cart fails entirely for one short line; "ship what's available" is a product choice
CANCELLATION IS THE SYMMETRIC OPERATION
cancelOrder(id) → order.cancel() (refused once DELIVERED), then for
each OrderItem: product.releaseStock(item.getQuantity()).
Without this, inventory leaks on every cancellation and the two paths drift.
reserve and release must be written as a pair, or neither is correct ✓
note: releaseStock re-adds to the SAME AtomicInteger tryReserve decremented
INSIDE tryReserve — check-then-act vs CAS
BEFORE — textbook check-then-act
if (quantity > stockQuantity) throw ...;
stockQuantity -= quantity;
Thread A reads stock = 1. Thread B reads stock = 1.
Both pass the check. Both decrement. Stock is now −1, or 0
with two orders shipped against one unit.
the read and the write are two steps, and anything can happen between them
AFTER — compare and swap, one atomic step
public boolean tryReserve(int quantity) {
while (true) {
int current = stockQuantity.get();
if (current < quantity) return false;
if (stockQuantity.compareAndSet(current, current - quantity)) return true; } }
The loop is not a spin lock — it retries only when another thread
SUCCEEDED, so the system always makes progress.
CAS covers ONE field. The rating average needed synchronized instead — choose per field ✓
MEASURED — 100 buyers, 1 unit of stock
The original checkout never consulted or decremented stock at all:
stock at start = 1 · orders placed = 100 · stock now = 1
*** OVERSOLD: 100 orders for 1 unit ***
after the CAS + saga: orders placed = 1, stock now = 0 ✓
The services also printed 100 lines of "Order created:" — a service layer that prints is not a library.
THE SAME IDEA, ONE LAYER DOWN
UPDATE product SET stock = stock − ? WHERE id = ? AND stock >= ?
… then check the affected-row count. compareAndSet and WHERE stock >= ? are the same idea.
SAY IT OUT LOUD:
"Reserve stock before the order exists, record every reservation so you can undo it, and make the compare-and-decrement one atomic step. Everything else is scaffolding."
WHY RESERVE AT CHECKOUT AND NOT AT ADD-TO-CART?
Reserving at add-to-cart lets an abandoned cart hold inventory hostage — which then needs an expiresAt and a sweeper thread.
Reserving at checkout needs neither, at the cost of a customer discovering at the last step that an item went out of stock.
Amazon reserves at order placement. Same choice here — and it's a clarifying question, not an assumption.
THE FLASH-SALE FOLLOW-UP (say the number)
One AtomicInteger for a viral product is a single contended cache line. Shard the counter into N buckets and reserve from a bucket,
or put a queue in front and admit buyers in order.
CAS contention starts to hurt in the thousands-of-threads range — not at 100.
LEGEND

g.text: Invariants defended: never oversell · all-or-nothing checkout · no leaked reservation · cancel returns stock · exact money (BigDecimal)
Honest gaps: compensation is not crash-safe · payment always approves · search is an O(n) scan · no JUnit harness for the oversell test yet
